issue.title: Descriptor-only Linux host platform profile for the end-station generators
issue.body:
The end-station generators (ADP/AEM descriptors, entity.conf) only accept FPGA platforms whose gPTP owner is the fabric. A Linux board running the control firmware as a host daemon (CPTS PHC, gPTP in a host daemon) cannot generate its descriptor image, so its daemon advertises AEM_SUPPORTED without a Configuration (IEEE 1722.1-2021 7.2.1). Tracked on the board side as kebag-logic/ti-sitara-am65x-bsp#29.

Scope:
- A descriptor-only Linux host platform profile: gPTP owner = host PHC. It feeds the existing ADP/AEM generators.
- All AEM and Milan checks run unchanged. FPGA profile validation is unchanged.
- No RTL or firmware-core change. Every FPGA generated artifact stays byte-identical (1x1/1if, 8x8/1if, Arty).
- A (1 interface, 1 source, 2 sinks) scheduling entry for the Linux build only, if it is needed. The FPGA scheduler-shape guard and its rows are untouched.

Stream inventory for the first user: one AAF input (48 kHz, 8 ch, 32-bit), one CRF input and one AAF output (Milan v1.2 7.2.2). No CRF output, because there is no second AAF input (7.2.3).

Acceptance:
- The profile generates a descriptor image and entity.conf that pass the generators' AEM checks.
- The FPGA artifacts' identity gate passes.
- Docs (ENDSTATION_BUILDER) describe the profile.
issue.display_title: Descriptor-only Linux host platform profile for the end-station generators

scope.body:
[A10] Ruling on the round-1 STOP.

(a) The upstream change is authorized as its own milan-fpga issue: kebag-logic/milan-fpga#983.
- A descriptor-only Linux host profile, gPTP owner = host PHC.
- All AEM/Milan checks and FPGA profile validation unchanged.
- No RTL or firmware-core change; FPGA artifacts byte-identical.
- A (1,1,2) scheduling entry for the Linux build only.

(b) Stream inventory:
- STREAM_INPUT 0: AAF, 48 kHz, 8 ch, 32-bit.
- STREAM_INPUT 1: CRF.
- STREAM_OUTPUT 0: AAF, same format.
- No second AAF and no CRF output; ADP counts become 1 source, 2 sinks.

Why: IEEE 1722.1-2021 7.2.1 needs a Configuration, and an AAF talker needs a CRF input (Milan v1.2 7.2.2). The daemon serves no CRF output and no second AAF stream, and 2/2 would only compile by advertising a stream nothing serves.

Next round:
- Land milan-fpga#983 first, then the pin, generation and AECP integration.
- Then make check, the firmware gate, veth enumeration and the aarch64 build.
- If the daemon cannot clock from the CRF input, that is recorded, and no Milan conformance is claimed for the board.

pr.body:
## Status

READY FOR REVIEW, local evidence only: `pf-linuxprof-1` -> `dev-soft-core`, two commits on `854bd7236792ce1adbd10c43b13a6a5002ad3bb6`: `677d605f37c3a80654df1dd2cde053b57242845b` (round 1) and `66b4def34dcbc0d371ce4eb339d3d0226875befa` (round 2, answering R900-1).

Published head: `677d605f37c3a80654df1dd2cde053b57242845b`. Round 2's head `66b4def34dcbc0d371ce4eb339d3d0226875befa` is committed locally and becomes the published head when it is pushed. The evidence below is local source-head evidence; hosted acceptance is tracked separately.

Round 2 (at `66b4def3`): gates 32, 41, 42 and `test_bad_configs_rejected` pass. Docs and quality gates: 24 of 24 pass. FPGA artifact identity: 245 of 245 byte-identical to the base and to `677d605f`, over 5 configs at own, split and all-fabric placements. Round 1 (at `677d605f`): builder suite 114 of 115 gates pass, each run once in four subsets; gate 1b did not complete inside the ten-minute command bound (see limitations). The full suite was not re-run at `66b4def3`.

## Linked Issue / roles

Closes #983
Relates to kebag-logic/ti-sitara-am65x-bsp#29

Executor: `[A830]`
Internal cleared-context reviewer: to be assigned
External reviewer: `[R900]` (round R900-1 NEGATIVE at `677d605f`; round 2 answers it)

## Description

A descriptor-only host profile for the end-station generators. It covers a board that runs the split control firmware as a host program on the mailbox model (`sw/firmware/ctrl/host/mbx_model.c`), with its own PHC as gPTP owner.

| Piece | Change |
|---|---|
| `sw/builder/endstation_builder.py` | `board.target: host` (`HOST_TARGET`), outside `BOARDS`. `load_config` reads the target with `_req`, as `_load_board` does, so a `board` that is a list or a string is refused by the same `ConfigError` as before the profile. The profile has its own board loader (`board.gptp_owner: host-phc`, `board.constraints.link_mbps`/`num_queues`), its own gPTP loader (every Announce field and `port_number` stated, latency corrections refused) and the `usb_audio` interface family (`HOST_INTERFACES`, width from `audio_interface.channels`). It has no SoC, fabric blocks, render-lane bound or framer supply cap. Every other loader and check is the FPGA path's, unchanged. `build()` refuses the profile by name. An FPGA target that names `board.gptp_owner` is now refused instead of ignored. The FPGA features block moved into `_load_fabric_features` unchanged. |
| `configs/host/endstation_host_example.yaml` | The annotated example: #983's first inventory. One AAF input (48 kHz, 8 ch, 32-bit), one CRF input and one AAF output; ADP 1 source, 2 sinks. It is outside `configs/endstation_*.yaml`, so no FPGA gate enumerates it. |
| `sw/firmware/ctrl/loop/ctrl_loop.h` | THE SHAPES gains `#elif defined(CTRL_HOST_PLATFORM) && CTRL_LOOP_SHAPE(1u, 1u, 2u)`. Its figures are 1x1/1if's, held as a stated host scheduling profile; the comment says what that profile claims and what it does not. The FPGA rows and the `#error` are untouched. No build input in this tree defines the macro, and gate 41 holds that. |
| `sw/builder/test_builder.py` | Gate 41: the example feeds the overlay, the AEM image (packer lint), `adp_entity.py`, `aecp_entity.py` and `srp_entity.py`, which agree with each other. ENTITY serves 1/2 and AVB_INTERFACE carries the stated dataset octet for octet. `build()` refuses the profile. THE SHAPES builds (1, 1, 2) with the macro alone, and the macro moves no listed FPGA row. Section 6's key table is held to the host loaders, gate 32's twin. The host TSpec rule is held too: a talker whose current format is 2 channels and which advertises 2 and 8 reserves the 8-channel 217 octets, not 73. Gate 42: 31 planted defects, 8 on the FPGA 1x1 (three malformed `board` values, five missing-fabric-owner and retarget cases) and 23 on the host example. `_key_map_rows` takes an optional heading; gate 32's call is unchanged. |
| `docs/ENDSTATION_BUILDER.md` | New section 6: the profile, what it feeds, what is unchanged, the keys that differ, the TSpec rule and its clause, the station MAC substitution a board owns, and the host shape row. Row 5d for `board.gptp_owner`. The section 3 Contents counts are corrected to the table's (75 rows, 116 keys), from the stale 66 and 107. |

**The host TSpec rule.** MaxFrameSize uses the widest `channels_per_frame` any talker advertises (`framer_declared_channels`). Every talker row shares that width at `clocking.sampling_rate_hz`. It is not each talker's current format. The clause is IEEE 802.1Q-2018 35.2.2.8.4 a): MaxFrameSize is "the maximum frame size that the Talker will produce".
- The control firmware declares one fixed TSpec per source (`ctrl_plat.c` `configure_sources`).
- SET_STREAM_FORMAT moves a STREAM_OUTPUT that is not streaming to any format it advertises (`aecp_commands.c`), and the declaration stays in place.
- MSRP changes no FirstValue of a declared StreamID short of a withdrawal and two LeaveAllTime periods (35.2.2.8).

So the widest advertised format's frame is one the talker can produce. Milan v1.2 4.3.3.2 Table 4.4 gives each format's value, and the profile takes the largest. The FPGA path keeps its supply cap because its fabric emits a fixed width. Round 2 changed the documentation of this rule, not the calculation. The generated image for the board's `config/endstation_pb2_bridge.yaml` (kebag-logic/ti-sitara-am65x-bsp at `cce8c9a4`) is unchanged: 5784 bytes, the same sha256, talker MaxFrameSize 217.

Material assumption, stated rather than chosen privately: the tracked tree is bare-metal only (#259, `scripts/check_baremetal_only.py`). So the profile and its fixtures use the tree's existing host-program vocabulary, never the retired-stack terms. No tracked YAML carries a false `fabric_gptp`; the host profile has no such key. Planted defects are written to temporary files at test time. The bare-metal scope gate passes on the head (0 findings over 1909 files, self-test 867 arms).

## Authoritative references

- IEEE 1722.1-2021 7.2.1 (a Configuration descriptor is required), 7.2.8 and Table 7-13 (AVB_INTERFACE gPTP fields), Table 7-2 (ENTITY fields repeat ADP's).
- Milan v1.2 7.2.2 (an AAF talker requires a CRF input), 7.2.3 (two AAF inputs require a CRF output), 5.3.3.4, 5.3.3.6, 5.3.3.9, 6.4; 4.3.3.2 Table 4.4 (MaxFrameSize per format).
- IEEE 802.1Q-2018 35.2.2.8.4 a) (MaxFrameSize: the maximum frame the Talker will produce), 35.2.2.8 (no FirstValue change for a declared StreamID short of a withdrawal and two LeaveAllTime periods).
- IEEE 802.1AS-2011 8.1 (domain 0), 8.6.2.3; IEEE 1588-2008 7.6.2.5 Table 6.
- `docs/ENDSTATION_BUILDER.md` sections 3 and 6; `ctrl_loop.h` THE SHAPES.

## How to get into the same state

```sh
git fetch origin && git checkout pf-linuxprof-1   # head 66b4def34dcbc0d371ce4eb339d3d0226875befa once pushed
git submodule update --init third_party/verilog-axis protocol-processor gptp-processor third_party/tsn-c-stack third_party/lwSRP
python3 -m pip install --require-hashes -r tools/markdown/requirements.txt && python3 -m pip install pyyaml
```

## How to validate

```sh
python3 sw/builder/test_builder.py --gates test_builder_doc_key_map,test_host_profile_feeds_the_generators,test_host_profile_refusals
python3 sw/builder/test_builder.py --gates test_bad_configs_rejected
for t in adp/adp_entity aecp/aecp_entity srp/srp_entity; do
  python3 sw/firmware/ctrl/$t.py configs/host/endstation_host_example.yaml -o /tmp/$(basename $t).h; done
python3 sw/builder/endstation_builder.py configs/host/endstation_host_example.yaml   # refused by name, exit 1
python3 scripts/check_baremetal_only.py --check && python3 scripts/docs_check.py
python3 scripts/check_em_dash.py --base 854bd7236792ce1adbd10c43b13a6a5002ad3bb6
python3 scripts/check_py_idiom.py
```

Expected:
- Gate 32: 116 keys == 116.
- Gate 41: two report lines, the first ending "a talker advertising 2 and 8 channels at current 2 reserves 217 octets, the widest format's, not the current 73".
- Gate 42: 31/31 refused (8 FPGA, 23 host).
- The three headers carry ADP 1/2, `CTRL_SRP_SOURCES 1u`/`CTRL_SRP_SINKS 2u`, and the image CRC.
- Every gate exits 0.

FPGA identity, at base, `677d605f` and `66b4def3` on the same tree: every `configs/endstation_*.yaml` is built at its own placement, `split` and `all-fabric`. Each revision's builder blob is loaded against unchanged dependencies. That covers the builder outputs, the sweep script, the AEM image pair and the four firmware generator headers (adp, aecp, srp, ctrl_plat policy). All 245 artifacts are byte-identical across the three revisions, and the tracked tree is clean.

## Known limitations / out of scope

- Gate 1b (`test_baremetal_profile_contract`, the builder's leg 0) did not complete in round 1. It runs one gate past the ten-minute bound on every command here. Its builder-dependent arms printed PASS (5 product configs, 11 refusal arms) before the bound; its remaining arms read firmware, SoC and RTL sources this change does not touch. The hosted `docs` and `elaborate` legs owe it.
- Round 2 re-ran only the gates its change touches (32, 41, 42, `test_bad_configs_rejected`), the 24 docs and quality gates, and the identity gate. The full builder suite at `66b4def3` is owed with the final candidate.
- `ci_builder_legs.py`'s own union was not used, because each leg exceeds the bound. Round 1's four subset receipts were judged by a lane-local script instead: every other gate ran exactly once and passed. The one NOT RUN row is gate 11's calibration report, which is not on this machine.
- The firmware gate's four shards each exceed the bound. In their place, at round 1:
  - `ctrl_loop.h` is token- and macro-identical at base and head for no shape header, 1x1 and 8x8.
  - The three Arty shapes are refused at both, and their diagnostics differ only in the `#error`'s line, 397 to 424.
  - The arms that read THE SHAPES or compose AECP and the platform ran on the gate's own tree and passed: service bounds and every-shape SRP builds with RV32 (21), AECP (18), split platform (8).
  - The mutation campaigns (shards 1 to 3) were not run.

  Round 2 touches no firmware.
- A `board` that cannot be iterated (`null`, an integer) raises TypeError at the base and still does. That is base behaviour, outside the host dispatch, and not changed here.
- The host shape row is a stated scheduling profile, not a measurement, and no board measurement is claimed. Its millisecond bounds rest on thread preemption, which nothing here measures.
- The profile does not build, package or install the host program; that is the board repository's (kebag-logic/ti-sitara-am65x-bsp#29).

## Definition of Done

- [x] Linked Issue acceptance criteria are satisfied (profile generates image and ADP fields through the AEM checks; identity gate; docs)
- [x] New or changed behavior has self-checking tests (gates 41, 42; each check has a planted control, and the round 2 additions fail at `677d605f` or under a mutant)
- [ ] Required local verification bar passes (gate 1b and the firmware mutation shards not completed here; full builder suite not re-run at `66b4def3`)
- [ ] Self-test evidence is posted in a PR comment
- [x] No undocumented requirement or interface change remains
- [ ] Internal cleared-context review is positive
- [ ] External review is positive (R900-1 NEGATIVE at `677d605f`; re-review of `66b4def3` pending)
- [ ] Blocking and major findings are fixed and re-reviewed (R900-1's two MINOR findings and the residue addressed at `66b4def3`; re-review pending)
- [ ] No review round remains in flight
- [ ] Candidate merge result is validated per CONTRIBUTING.md
- [x] Documentation is updated where needed
- [ ] Post-merge containment will be checked before the Issue moves to Done

[A10] INDEPENDENT REVIEW STARTED: R900-1

R900 (external reviewer) reconstructs issue #983 / PR #986 at exact head `677d605f37c3a80654df1dd2cde053b57242845b`, tree `79d523167a95861b8092b64574222db91bce5a07`, in a cleared context from public scope, requirements, diff and evidence, applying all five lenses with a reviewer-owned ledger. No source edits or merge while this review runs; merge still requires two independent positive reviews and the full completion bar.

[R900] NEGATIVE - exact head 677d605f37c3a80654df1dd2cde053b57242845b

External independent review R900-1 of issue #983 / PR #986. All five lenses were applied. Two MINOR findings remain open. Under the assigned completion rule they prevent a positive verdict and leave their attributable lenses unclean. One separate RESIDUE concerns stale PR publication wording.

Reviewed tree: `79d523167a95861b8092b64574222db91bce5a07`. Source base: `854bd7236792ce1adbd10c43b13a6a5002ad3bb6`. One commit changes five files. This is a source-head review, not validation of a merge into current dev.

## Authorities and independence

Reconstructed from AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/README.md, [issue #983](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/983), its public acceptance/evidence comment, and the [scope ruling on board issue #29](https://github.com/kebag-logic/ti-sitara-am65x-bsp/issues/29#issuecomment-7096504049). Then examined REQUIREMENTS.md sections 1 and 8, docs/overview/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/reference/PP_DESCRIPTOR_OWNERSHIP.md, ENDSTATION_BUILDER, the exact diff/history, and the [published author packet](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/tree/adeb1331026950e5c13c31debb44a225caa62ad1/review-evidence/linuxprof-r1).

The issue and ruling authorize a descriptor-only extension. They do not restore an FPGA operating-system product path forbidden by [#259](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/259). The target has no gateware build, fabric-owner substitution, or software installation path. Its spelling `host` follows existing portable-host terminology; the unchanged bare-metal scope gate passes.

No private author material or other reviewer's report was read. [independent-verdict.md](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/ee13b4233fcb9ce2adcc220de9265a79e88a6589/review-evidence/linuxprof-r1/reviews/R900-1/independent-verdict.md) records the independent findings and ledger before prior-review retrieval. Subsequent retrieval found zero submitted reviews, zero inline review threads, and only the review-start conversation comment. There are no prior public findings to resolve or retain. [public-state.json](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/ee13b4233fcb9ce2adcc220de9265a79e88a6589/review-evidence/linuxprof-r1/reviews/R900-1/public-state.json) records the consulted public state.

## Findings

### R900-1-F1

[R900] MINOR Conformance / Robustness / Tests - `sw/builder/endstation_builder.py:4801`; `sw/builder/test_builder.py:30804` - Host dispatch bypasses the existing malformed-board refusal boundary.

**Authority/evidence:** Issue #983 requires unchanged FPGA profile validation. `load_config()` explicitly promises ConfigError on a violation at lines 4788-4789. Starting with the valid FPGA 1x1 config, replace only `board` with `[]`, `""`, or `["ax7101"]`. At the source base all three return `ConfigError: board: missing required key 'target'`. At the reviewed head all three raise AttributeError from the new unconditional `brd.get("target")`. The ADP generator CLI handles ConfigError but not AttributeError (`sw/firmware/ctrl/adp/adp_entity.py:106`). Gate 42 exercises keys inside a mapping, not this container boundary. See [regression-result.json](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/ee13b4233fcb9ce2adcc220de9265a79e88a6589/review-evidence/linuxprof-r1/reviews/R900-1/regression-result.json) and [regression.log](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/ee13b4233fcb9ce2adcc220de9265a79e88a6589/review-evidence/linuxprof-r1/reviews/R900-1/regression.log).

**Impact:** Malformed input escapes the documented validation interface and crashes callers that correctly catch ConfigError. This does not accept invalid configurations or change valid FPGA artifacts; severity is MINOR.

**Required outcome:** Host dispatch must preserve controlled ConfigError refusal for these malformed board values. Add a discriminating regression test, retaining valid FPGA/host controls and the missing-fabric-owner plants.

**Verification:** Re-run `regression_probe.py` and require ConfigError for all three inputs at the corrected head. Gates 41/42 must stay green, and the added regression must fail against `677d605f`.

### R900-1-F2

[R900] MINOR Docs - `docs/ENDSTATION_BUILDER.md:1248`; `sw/builder/endstation_builder.py:4815` - Host TSpec is documented as current-format-derived, but uses the widest advertised talker format.

**Authority/evidence:** The new section says, “SRP's TSpec takes the declared current format.” The adjacent source explanation also describes each talker's current format. Line 4818 instead calls `framer_declared_channels()`, whose lines 1184-1200 maximize channel width across every format of every talker. `_srp_rows()` applies that shared width at `clocking.sampling_rate_hz`. An accepted host variant with a two-channel current format and two/eight-channel supported formats produces MaxFrameSize **217**; its current-format geometry is **73**. The variant packs successfully into a 4,784-byte image. See [regression-result.json](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/ee13b4233fcb9ce2adcc220de9265a79e88a6589/review-evidence/linuxprof-r1/reviews/R900-1/regression-result.json).

**Impact:** The documented rule predicts a different reservation size and bandwidth than the generator computes. This is an incorrect protocol-field derivation claim, not cosmetic wording; it is MINOR rather than RESIDUE. No defect in the conservative calculation itself is established here.

**Required outcome:** Describe the actual shared maximum across advertised AAF talker formats, at the configured sampling rate, without claiming it is each stream's current-format geometry. Correct the section and source explanation. No calculation change is requested.

**Verification:** The current-two/supported-two-and-eight fixture retains its measured 217-byte result, and both explanations match `framer_declared_channels()` and `_srp_rows()`.

### R900-1-R1

[R900] RESIDUE Docs - [PR #986 body, Status](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/986) - Publication wording predates the published PR.

**Authority/evidence:** The body says “Not pushed; no hosted run exists yet.” The PR exposes the reviewed head, and the hosted snapshot contains four queued runs. No successful or executed job is inferred.

**Impact:** Stale publication wording only; no measurement, generated artifact, test, conformance claim, or verdict changes. It does not leave an additional lens unclean.

**Exact fix:** Replace that sentence with: “Published head: `677d605f37c3a80654df1dd2cde053b57242845b`. The evidence below is local source-head evidence; hosted acceptance is tracked separately.”

**Verification:** Compare the sentence with the PR head. Preserve the existing incomplete-gate disclosures.

## Five-lens results

**Conformance:** The host branch rejoins existing entity, clocking, stream, format, SRP, platform, cluster and identity code. Its owner is exactly `host-phc`; fabric features and SoC declarations refuse. The unchanged domain-zero and clockAccuracy validators run. The Configuration descriptor exists. The 5,784-byte image contains AAF input 0, CRF input 1 and AAF output 0, no CRF output, and ENTITY/ADP counts 1/2. AAF format is `0x0205022002006000`; CRF is `0x041060010000BB80`. These match #983 and the board ruling's inventory. F1 leaves the validation-contract portion unclean.

The `entity.conf` acceptance path is real and board-owned. At public board commit `cce8c9a4143548c80800b2def821431ff45e3698`, `milan-linux/tools/gen-entity-conf.sh` calls this checkout's unchanged `adp_entity.py`. It generated correct values for the PR example and board YAML. The latter matches every published entity.conf value, including model ID `0x001BC50AC1000100`, counts 1/2 and capabilities `0xC588`, `0x4001`, `0x4801`. Only the exported-tree revision comment requires normalization because this clone lacks `.milan-fpga-rev`. [entity-conf-result.json](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/ee13b4233fcb9ce2adcc220de9265a79e88a6589/review-evidence/linuxprof-r1/reviews/R900-1/entity-conf-result.json) names exact public inputs and output hashes. This proves generation, not daemon or board behavior.

[R900] PASS RTL - `source.diff`; `sw/firmware/ctrl/loop/ctrl_loop.h:353`; [identity-result.json](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/ee13b4233fcb9ce2adcc220de9265a79e88a6589/review-evidence/linuxprof-r1/reviews/R900-1/identity-result.json); [shape-result.json](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/ee13b4233fcb9ce2adcc220de9265a79e88a6589/review-evidence/linuxprof-r1/reviews/R900-1/shape-result.json) - No RTL, firmware C implementation, hardware interface, or submodule gitlink changes. The authorized scheduler-header row is the sole firmware delta. Clock/reset/CDC and datapath contracts are untouched. All **245** independently captured FPGA builder/image/header artifacts match base/head across five configs at own, explicit split and explicit all-fabric placements. The comparison loads each exact builder blob against unchanged dependencies without replacing tracked files. Existing scheduler token/macro outputs and refusal outcomes match across twelve config/interface selections. The host loop translation unit compiles with strict warnings and its static assertions.

The `(1,1,2)` row requires `CTRL_HOST_PLATFORM`. Gate 41 proves refusal without it, unchanged listed FPGA rows with it, and no definition in this repository's build inputs. Its figures reuse 1x1/1if, justified as a stated profile with one fewer talker and unchanged sinks. The comment excludes measurement of descriptor-dependent costs and host preemption. This supports the stated conditional profile, not a measured host timing guarantee.

**Robustness:** Gate 42 passes 28 input plants, including five FPGA separation/owner cases. Independent probes cover all nine required gPTP declarations, integer extrema and wrong types, link rates, queue counts, interface widths and clockAccuracy values. Sixteen valid gPTP extrema survive into descriptor bytes. Existing packed-image L6/L10 cases were additionally applied to the host, including malformed offsets, empty/excess/partial arrays and required descriptor removal. Removing host-owner validation in memory makes the new refusal test fail. [boundary-result.json](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/ee13b4233fcb9ce2adcc220de9265a79e88a6589/review-evidence/linuxprof-r1/reviews/R900-1/boundary-result.json) records 119 observations. F1 remains open.

**Tests:** Gates 32/41/42 pass: 116 documented FPGA keys, 64 host keys, three agreeing generators, the macro guard and 28 refusals. Independent evidence adds FPGA identity, scheduler preprocessing, entity.conf generation, host-loop compilation and boundary/packer negative controls. The image probe accumulates index-map runs to locate the differently sized AAF/CRF descriptors. F1 needs a committed regression before Tests can be clean.

**Docs:** ENDSTATION_BUILDER section 6 describes the profile, key differences, no-build boundary, runtime MAC integration duty and unmeasured scheduling assumptions. No added source comment contains a prohibited bench lane label, review round, reviewer ID or issue-comment ID. `docs_check`, bare-metal check/self-test, document paths and the em-dash gate pass. F2 leaves Docs unclean despite these mechanical passes. R1 is publication residue.
